item.title: Nigeria needs 9% annual growth to reduce poverty – Soludo
item.description: Governor Chukwuma Soludo of Anambra says Nigeria needs an annual economic growth of at least nine per cent to significantly reduce poverty and create jobs. He made the assertion at the Nigerian Economic Summit 32 (NES32) with the theme “Growth that Works: Delivering Jobs, Productivity and Shared Prosperity” in Abuja on Monday. He said that Nigeria’s current growth rate of about four per cent remained inadequate to achieve rapid poverty reduction and employment generation. The governor also said that Nigeria would require an annual growth of at least 12 per cent to achieve a one-trillion-dollar economy by 2030 or 2040. He added that the country’s investment rate, estimated at 17 to 20 per cent, must rise significantly to support the required economic expansion. Soludo cautioned against being misled by large nominal spending figures, saying that consolidated public expenditure across all government levels amounted to less than one dollar per person daily. He stressed the need to channel national savings into productive investments, capable of expanding economic output, creating jobs and improving living standards. He called for stronger coordination between the federal government, states and local governments, noting that subnational authorities accounted for a substantial share of public spending. According to him, effective collaboration is essential to maximise the impact of government policies and investments across the country. Soludo cited Anambra’s free education programme, which covers kindergarten through secondary school, as an example of interventions delivering measurable social benefits. He said that the state had reduced its out-of-school children rate from 2.5 per cent to 0.25 per cent. He also cited a recent Oxford and United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) report which reportedly placed Anambra’s multidimensional poverty rate at 9.6 per cent. Soludo said that reducing food prices required structural reforms to address post-harvest losses, which he put at about 43 per cent of agricultural output. He said that improving storage, transportation and distribution systems would help to move food from farms to urban markets and reduce consumer prices. The governor, therefore, urged governments to strengthen sectoral collaboration and mobilise investments to accelerate economic growth. Soludo also called for policies that encourage exports, develop domestic value chains and promote investment in sectors where Nigeria has competitive advantages. He emphasised that stronger private-sector participation and productive investments were essential to generating sustainable jobs and ensuring that economic growth benefitted more Nigerians. item.title: Northern leaders must share blame for region’s backwardness – Gov Uba Sani
item.description: Kaduna State Governor, Uba Sani, has said political office holders in Northern Nigeria since 1999 must accept responsibility for the region’s developmental challenges, including its high number of out-of-school children. Sani made the remarks while defending President Bola Tinubu’s record in office, arguing that Northern leaders should not blame the current administration alone for problems that have persisted for decades. “I’m a northerner, and I’m telling you that anybody who held position, whether a governor, minister, senator, vice president, you should be ready to take blame,” he said. The governor cited figures on out-of-school children, stating that Nigeria had about 18 million children out of school as of 2023, with approximately 70 per cent living in Northern Nigeria. He questioned whether Tinubu, who assumed office in May 2023, should be held solely responsible for a crisis that predates his administration. Sani also disclosed that Kaduna State had about 550,000 out-of-school children when he assumed office in 2023, claiming that his administration had returned 300,000 of them to classrooms. He urged political leaders to move away from regional sentiments in their campaigns, insisting that voters should assess candidates based on their records in public office rather than their geographical origins. “The people of Northern Nigeria are very smart. You cannot come to them and tell them, ‘Vote for me because I’m a northerner.’ They will never vote for you. They can only vote for you based on your track record,” he said. The governor also highlighted federal road projects in the North-East and North-West as evidence of infrastructure development under Tinubu. According to him, more than 348 kilometres of roads had been completed in the North-East, while about 3,100 kilometres were under construction. He added that approximately 1,800 kilometres of the ongoing projects were nearing 90 per cent completion. In the North-West, Sani said more than 342 kilometres of roads had been completed, while another 1,042 kilometres were nearing 90 per cent completion. On education financing, the governor said more than 414,000 students from the North-West had benefited from the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), with about N84 billion allocated to the region. He described the student loan scheme as an intervention for young people from low-income households who might otherwise struggle to finance their education. Sani further stressed the importance of technical and vocational education and training (TVET), saying skills development was essential to addressing unemployment and expanding opportunities for young people in Northern Nigeria. He maintained that education remained critical to the region’s development and urged political leaders to focus on policies and programmes that improve the lives of residents. item.title: Nigeria’s Index Ebola Patient, Husband Evacuated To Switzerland – Pate
item.description: Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Ali Pate, on Monday confirmed that the first imported Ebola virus disease case in the country has been flown out of the country to Switzerland. Pate made the confirmation on his X handle, stating that the index patient, who has clinically improved, is stable and conscious, was evacuated along with her husband, who remained asymptomatic. He wrote: “I confirm that, with my approval, earlier this morning, the index case for Nigeria’s first imported Ebola virus disease departed Abuja for Switzerland. The index patient was clinically much improved, stable, conscious, communicating, and her clinical laboratory test results closing towards baseline. He, however, stated that her improvements do not mean she is not infectious, stating that strict protocols were put in place before her evacuation. “This does not mean she is not still infectious, hence the strict protocols in place. The patient was evacuated along with her spouse who has remained asymptomatic. ‘I thank all the various clinical staff for the high quality care they provided the patient as well as the public health personnel who ensured the evacuation was carried out in line with best public health measures for such evacuations. “We will provide further updates later this afternoon after the patient and her spouse lands successfully in their destination. “All public health measures are continuing to ensure successful containment of the imported virus. “I urge Nigerians to remain vigilant and rely on information from credible sources”, Pate said. The development came after the Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), on Sunday, said that the number of contacts linked to the index case of Ebola recorded in October 2026 had risen to 53. The agency said the contacts comprise health workers as well as the domestic staff and spouse of the patient diagnosed with the disease. The NCDC, in its Ebola Disease Situation Report, said that a newly suspected case was reported by Rivers State on October 23, but laboratory results returned negative for Ebola disease. “Fifty-three contacts linked to the index case have so far been identified, categorized and followed up. Contacts listed include healthcare workers, domestic staff and spouse,” the report dated October 24, 2026, partly read. Giving a background on the index case, it said the patient is a 42-year-old woman who returned from Uganda through Addis Ababa on October 3, 2026, via an international flight to Abuja, Nigeria. The agency said she became symptomatic four days later and presented to a private health facility on October 10, and another on October 11. “She presented to another private facility on the 11th of October 2026, where she was admitted. The NCDC was notified on the 19th of October, followed by in-depth case investigation and sample collection,” it said. “A confirmation by the NCDC National Reference Laboratory was made on 20th October 2026. item.title: Delta: Police arrest school bus driver over alleged kidnap, assault of 14-year-old
item.description: By Emmauel Okogba The Delta State Police Command has arrested a 28-year-old school bus driver, Onome Lucky Ughagha, over the alleged kidnapping and sexual assault of a 14-year-old female student in Sapele. The suspect was also accused of demanding and collecting ₦503,000 from the victim’s father as ransom before abandoning the girl along Oton Road, Sapele. The police said the incident was reported at the Sapele Area Command on October 20, 2026, by the victim’s father, who alleged that the suspect abducted his daughter while she was preparing to leave for school. According to a statement by the Police Public Relations Officer, Delta State Command, SP Bright Edafe, the suspect allegedly contacted the girl’s father, demanded ₦503,000 and threatened to kill the minor if the money was not paid. The statement said the victim was abandoned along Oton Road after the ransom was paid and subsequently reunited with her family in a traumatised condition, with indications that she had been sexually assaulted. Following the report, operatives of the Sapele Area Command commenced investigations, while the victim was taken to a medical facility for examination and treatment. The police added that the school principal and vice principal were invited for questioning as efforts intensified to apprehend the suspect, who had allegedly abandoned the school bus and fled. Edafe said the suspect was eventually arrested on October 23 at his hideout in the Ajimele area of Sapele following intelligence-led operations. “During preliminary interrogation, he reportedly confessed to his involvement in the crime,” the statement said. The police disclosed that arrangements were underway to transfer the suspect to the State Criminal Investigation Department in Asaba for further investigation. The Commissioner of Police in Delta State, CP Samuel Erale, condemned the incident and reaffirmed the command’s commitment to protecting children from violence and exploitation. He assured that the investigation would be thorough and that anyone found culpable would be brought to justice. The commissioner also urged school authorities, parents and transport operators to strengthen measures to protect children, stressing that the safety of every child entrusted to their care must remain a priority. item.title: Macron says ‘social media is damaging our democracies’
item.description: President Emmanuel Macron said on Monday that social media was “damaging our democracies” as France struggled to contain weeks of protests marked by street violence and looting. He said on a visit to Marseille that social media was especially used during unrest on October 17 “to bring young and not-so-young people to places where criminal acts, attacks and looting were taking place”. item.title: Ondo Assembly passes bill for establishment of state police
item.description: Ondo State House of Assembly has passed a bill seeking to amend the 1999 Constitution to provide for the establishment of state police services. The bill was passed following deliberations by the lawmakers at a plenary session on Monday in Akure. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the proposal was conveyed to the assembly in a letter from the National Assembly Clerk, Kamoru Ogunlana, which was read by the Speaker, Olamide Oladiji, on Sept. 24. The House Leader, Olatunji Oshati, who moved for the passage and its transmission to the National Assembly, said the lawmakers had considered the implications of the proposed amendment for the citizenry. Oshati said that the establishment of state police would address the numerous security challenges confronting the country. The motion was seconded by Mr Allen Oluwatoyin, All Progressives Congress (APC), member representing Ese-Odo State Constituency. Also speaking, Oladiji described the proposed establishment of state police as long overdue, saying it would enable security agencies to respond more swiftly to crime and other security concerns. He noted that state policing, being grassroots-based, would reduce crime through improved intelligence gathering and proactive security measures. “There will be greater confidence in state policing. It will strengthen intelligence gathering and provide grassroots security,” he added. The speaker, however, commended the lawmakers for their contributions to the bill and its passage. It was gathered that the bill would be transmitted to the National Assembly for further legislative consideration. (NAN) The post Ondo Assembly passes bill for establishment of state police appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Video: Pastor marries 2nd wife, says ‘monogamy is unbiblical’
item.description: Pastor Israel Ford of LifeWorks Church in Wickliffe, Ohio, United States, has announced his marriage to a second wife, describing monogamy as unbiblical. In a post on Facebook, Pastor Ford supported his action with Exodus 21:10. The Bible reference says: “If he take him another wife; her food, her raiment, and her duty of marriage, shall he not diminish” (King James Version). A video accompanying the post has first wife, Prophetess Lydia Ford, introducing Minister Shakayla Ford as her husband’s second wife. She said they had been privately married for three years. Pastor Ford wrote: “I would like to introduce to the world, my second wife, Shakayla Ford. “As a nation, we have been taught that a man should have one wife only. This is unbiblical. “I encourage you to watch today’s sermon in its entirety. I understand that this is an unpopular truth that we have gotten away from and many Pastors will not preach. “I have no plans to choose pleasing man over what God has revealed. People may not accept this and choose to disconnect, and that is ok! “This life will be over soon and we can all laugh about it in Heaven. Until then, God bless.” An Ohio church stunned their congregration after its leadership team announced they are living in a polygynous marriage. item.title: Man Utd crisis deepens as Carrick faces axe
item.description: Winless in eight games and hovering just above the Premier League relegation zone, struggling Manchester United are facing the prospect of yet another managerial change, with Michael Carrick likely to pay the price. The former United midfielder was warmly applauded by fans as he made his way down the tunnel after his team’s chastening 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday. Moments later a chorus of boos erupted as the players left the pitch — with fans clear in their minds where the blame lies for United’s current malaise. Carrick was handed a two-year deal in May after inspiring an impressive revival following the team’s struggles under Ruben Amorim — United secured third place in the Premier League and a return to the Champions League. But a drastic decline this season is an all-too-familiar story for United supporters, who last witnessed a Premier League title triumph 13 years ago under Alex Ferguson. An emotional Carrick denied his lap of the pitch at full-time on Sunday was a goodbye as he struggles to come to terms with his team’s precipitous decline. “I definitely knew that we hadn’t cracked it and there was a lot of work to be done, but that doesn’t mean to say that it should have gone this way,” he said. Carrick, 45, is clinging on but his position appears increasingly precarious, with former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann apparently in the frame for the job. The United boss, who won multiple titles in the club’s golden era under Ferguson, was the seventh permanent appointment since the Scot retired. David Moyes was proven in the Premier League, Louis van Gaal and Jose Mourinho had stellar records and Erik ten Hag and Amorim were seen as rising stars of coaching. – Sentimental choice – Carrick is in the same category as Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, who was in charge for three years from 2018 — a sentimental choice as a former player who played a major role in the club’s glory years under Ferguson. “The Manchester United fans are singing the Michael Carrick song because I think they know what’s going to happen here. They’ve seen this before. He’s one of their own and he’s popular,” former United captain Gary Neville told Sky Sports. “But the owners, the sporting department and the players are not popular and they’ve badly let this football club down.” The problems at the club, as Neville points out, go far beyond the dugout. Despite fierce, ongoing protests from fans, the US-based Glazer family still hold a majority stake in the club Malcolm Glazer bought via a leveraged takeover in 2005, saddling United with huge debts. Any hopes that the arrival of British billionaire Jim Ratcliffe as a minority owner in 2024 would signal a new dawn have been dashed. Ratcliffe has overseen cost-cutting measures including widespread redundancies and ticket hikes but the club’s debt has still soared above £1.1 billion ($1.47 billion). item.title: US singer Chris Brown avoids jail over UK nightclub brawl
item.description: American R&B singer Chris Brown avoided jail when sentenced by a UK court Monday after pleading guilty to a public order offence during a 2023 brawl at a London nightclub. The former boyfriend of music sensation Rihanna was handed an eight-month jail sentence suspended for a year — meaning he will not be imprisoned unless he commits another offence during the period. Brown, 37, who was wearing a black face mask and black cap when he arrived Monday at Southwark Crown Court in London, had admitted to affray during an appearance in July. “Violence of this kind in a crowded nightclub is serious. It creates an obvious risk, not merely to the person against whom it is directed, but also to others,” judge Tony Baumgartner said, handing down the sentence. Prosecutors had accused him and co-defendant Omololu Akinlolu, also a US national, of carrying out “a vicious and unprovoked attack” in a crowded nightclub “where Brown used a glass bottle as a weapon to strike the victim’s head twice”. The guilty plea avoided a trial on several other charges, including attempting to cause grievous bodily harm with intent and possession of an offensive weapon, namely a bottle. Brown, who has sold tens of millions of records worldwide, had earlier denied those charges. All of the allegations relate to an incident at Tape, a private members’ club in central London, on February 19, 2023, while Brown was touring the UK. The victim was struck several times with a bottle before being pursued, punched and kicked. The singer is known for mid-2000s hits such as “Kiss, Kiss”, as well as a litany of legal troubles including a felony conviction for assaulting Rihanna in 2009. Brown rose from a local church choir in Virginia to sudden fame with his rich R&B voice before turning to rap. He was convicted of having beaten then-girlfriend Rihanna before the 2009 Grammy Awards, forcing the pop star to miss the annual gala. In 2012, Brown was involved in an altercation at a New York nightclub with members of hip hop star Drake’s entourage, during which French basketball player Tony Parker suffered an eye injury after being hit by a thrown glass bottle. Two years later, Brown pleaded guilty to assaulting a fan in Washington. Akinlolu, 40 also pleaded guilty to affray over the London incident. He was sentenced to four months’ imprisonment suspended for a year. The post US singer Chris Brown avoids jail over UK nightclub brawl appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Peter Obi demands supporter’s release, accuses Tinubu of undermining democracy
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi has demanded the release of party supporter Rilwan Olawale, accusing President Bola Tinubu of undermining democracy by “encouraging and facilitating violence.” In a statement posted on X on Monday, Obi described the reported incident as part of what he called the intimidation and harassment of his supporters. He also accused President Bola Tinubu of encouraging and facilitating violence, and demanded transparency over Olawale’s reported arrest, respect for his rights and an end to what he described as politically motivated harassment. “The continued intimidation and harassment of my supporters across the country, the latest being the case of Rilwan Olawale, is disturbing and unacceptable. “President Bola Tinubu has remained a huge beneficiary of our democracy and should not brazenly be destroying it by encouraging and facilitating violence.” Obi further stated that his campaign was peaceful and issue-driven, and warned that his supporters’ restraint should not be mistaken for weakness. “We have chosen the path of peace, not violence; persuasion, not intimidation. However, nobody should mistake our civility for weakness, our restraint for fear, or our commitment to peace for an absence of resolve. We will not be intimidated into silence, nor will we abandon Nigerians who believe in a New Nigeria that is possible and will be OK.” He called for Olawale’s release and said Nigerians should be free to support the candidate of their choice. “I therefore demand transparency regarding Rilwan Olawale’s arrest, his release, respect for his rights, and an end to politically motivated harassment. No government or political party has the right to deny Nigerians the freedom to support a candidate of their choice. “We will remain peaceful but resolute. We will not resort to violence, but we will stand firmly and lawfully against every attempt to undermine our democratic rights.” According to NDC’s Lagos governorship candidate, Funso Doherty, Olawale was reportedly taken from his residence at about 1 a.m. on Sunday by men who identified themselves as Department of State Services (DSS) operatives. Doherty, in a statement on his X handle on Sunday, said he was in contact with Olawale’s family and legal counsel, who were seeking to establish what happened and gain access to him. He said: “This afternoon, reports reached me that Mr. Rilwan Olawale, a strong NDC supporter, who is also identified with the Obidient movement, was allegedly picked up by some armed men who identified themselves as operatives of the Department of State Services in the very early hours of today, Sunday 25th October.” Doherty also urged the public to remain calm while the family and legal counsel sought information about Olawale’s whereabouts. item.title: Trump blasts Norway over Nobel Peace Prize snub
item.description: US President Donald Trump attacked Norway during a campaign rally, calling it a “shit house country,” and said that Norwegian immigrants were not welcome in the United States because its Nobel Committee had not awarded him the Peace Prize. “Frankly, Norway sucks. Norway has become a shit house country, actually,” he said during Sunday’s speech. Since returning to the White House in January 2025, Trump has made no secret of his desire to win the prestigious Nobel Peace prize. Judge and former UN rights chief Navi Pillay of South Africa was this year’s recipient of the prize. Trump has called the committee’s choice “a disgraceful and embarrassing decision” and argued that the award should have gone to him. Trump said Sunday he would welcome immigrants from certain countries but not Norway “because I didn’t get the Nobel Prize.” “So I don’t want anybody from Norway,” he said during the rally in the Michigan town of Port Huron ahead of crucial US midterm elections on November 3. There was no official indication of a new US policy on Norwegian immigrants. Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide responded to Trump’s comments about the Nobel prize on Monday, maintaining that the committee is independent. “He knows very well that the Nobel Committee is independent. We have reminded him of that, in case anyone is wondering – and that is still the case,” he told national broadcaster NRK. Trump came under fire in 2018, during his first term, after using similar vulgar expressions to refer to Haiti and certain African countries. item.title: Houthis attack Saudi Arabia before high-stakes talks in Tehran
item.description: Yemen’s Houthis have kept up their attacks on Saudi Arabia as senior officials from the kingdom, Turkey and Pakistan are due to hold high-stakes talks with Iran in Tehran on Monday, following warnings of a return to war. Fresh explosions rattled Riyadh overnight, along with a text message warning to residents, after the Iran-allied Houthis claimed a new attack on the Saudi capital’s international airport on Sunday. Saudi Arabia, the world’s top oil exporter, has become deeply embroiled in the eight-month war since hostilities in its long-running conflict with the Iran-allied Houthis resumed in July. Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman is among the delegations travelling to Tehran, made up of officials from the three countries that signed a defence alliance in Mecca in August. Their visit follows warnings by the United States, Iran and Israel that hostilities could resume. Tensions have increased ahead of Israel’s pivotal election on Tuesday and next week’s US mid-terms, where US President Donald Trump’s Republicans are battling to keep control of both chambers of the US Congress. Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei will take part in Monday’s meeting with Prince Khalid, Pakistani army chief General Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin, the deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, Ali Bagheri Kani, told state TV. “This historic meeting in Tehran may be the last chance before escalation spirals out of control, an attempt to impose a path of de-escalation before it’s too late,” Hesham Alghannam, a Saudi security analyst and researcher, posted on X. “The presence of military and security figures at this level together means that the remaining time is extremely limited.” – ‘Serious tensions’ – On Sunday, as blasts rang out over Riyadh and authorities sent texts warning residents of a “hostile aerial threat”, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it struck missile launchers and storage facilities in Yemen. The Houthis said they had attacked Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport once again. The repeatedly targeted facility has been largely closed since 13 people were killed and more than 300 wounded in a major attack this month. Mediation efforts between the US and Iran have been led by Qatar and Pakistan. A Qatari delegation visited Tehran on Sunday, Iran’s foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said. “Our region is in the grip of serious tensions, and neighbouring countries are striving to convey a message and put forward initiatives,” Baqaei said on Monday. Andreas Krieg of London-based risk consultancy MENA analytica said Prince Khalid’s presence in Tehran was “hugely significant”, calling him the “strategic mastermind of Saudi Arabia”. item.title: Luxury SUVs for APC youths insult to struggling Nigerians – Atiku slams Tinubu
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has described the reported distribution of luxury sport utility vehicles to All Progressives Congress (APC) youth leaders as an insult to Nigerians grappling with hunger and rising living costs. Atiku, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, called on President Bola Tinubu and the Presidency to explain the source of funding for the vehicles, reportedly 2026 models valued at more than N150m each. In a statement on Monday issued by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku questioned the reported donation of the vehicles by First Lady Oluremi Tinubu, saying Nigerians deserved to know who paid for them. “The APC National Youth Leader says these vehicles were donated by First Lady Oluremi Tinubu. Nigerians deserve to know where the money came from to buy and distribute so many 2026 model SUVs, each worth more than N150 million, for political mobilisation,” he said. Atiku asked whether the vehicles were purchased with the First Lady’s personal funds, donations or public resources, demanding that the Presidency disclose the total cost and source of the money. “The First Lady holds no elected or executive office. She is only a domestic appendage of the office of President. Were these vehicles bought with her personal funds, donations or public resources? Who paid for them? What was the total cost? The Presidency must provide a clear account,” the former vice-president said. He argued that the reported gifts were inappropriate at a time when many Nigerians were struggling to afford food, transportation and other basic necessities. “At a time families cannot afford food, transport and other basic necessities, these gifts are a brazen insult to the people. The government has found a way to provide luxury SUVs for APC youth leaders, yet millions of Nigerians are still waiting for meaningful relief from the cost of living crisis,” he said. Atiku also questioned the timing of the reported vehicle distribution, alleging that APC women leaders had previously received luxury vehicles and that the earlier gifts came shortly before the abduction of schoolchildren in Oyo State. He said the latest reported distribution raised concerns about the government’s spending priorities amid economic hardship and insecurity. “While Nigerians continue to ask where the savings from subsidy removal have gone, the Presidency must explain how such costly gifts are being funded. If the vehicles were paid for privately, the source of the funds should be disclosed. If public resources were used, the government must identify who authorised the spending and under what legal authority,” he said. The ADC presidential candidate further alleged that the scale of the reported gifts raised questions about whether wealth and public resources were being used to secure political loyalty. item.title: Ebola: Yobe Govt Activates Emergency Response Centres, Border Surveillance
item.description: The Yobe State government said it has not yet recorded any Ebola virus but has activated its Public Health Emergency Incident Management System and developed a comprehensive Emergency Preparedness and Response plan to monitor the possible outbreak of the disease. The Commissioner for Health, Dr. Mohammed Lawan Gana, represented by the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry, Hadiza Sabo, disclosed this while briefing journalists in Damaturu on Monday. According to her, the state government is building 6 technical pillars recommended by the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control for the Ebola Virus Disease response, which are coordinated through the Emergency Operations Centre (EOC). “Yobe State shares an international border; consequently, the state is strengthening cross-border surveillance and coordination with transport and relevant border authorities at key entry points to enhance vigilance, facilitate the timely detection and reporting of public health threats, and support prompt response to potential disease outbreaks” “We have outlined six pillars of coordination and management: epidemiology and surveillance, case management, infection prevention and control, laboratory services, communication and community engagement, as well as point of entry,” she said. Sabo further added that the government is intensifying public awareness campaigns using radio, television, community town carriers and engagement with traditional leaders. “Our message is simple; Ebola is real, but it is preventable and controllable. We are advising citizens to maintain good hand hygiene, avoid direct contact with the bodily fluids of anyone showing symptoms, and report any unusual illness or death to the nearest health facility immediately”. The government advises the general public to shun any rumours or misinformation and rely on verified information from the State Ministry of Health, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) and other official sources, and not to spread unverified reports on social media, as doing that can cause unnecessary panic and harm. item.title: Ebola: Plateau reactivates isolation centres, strengthens surveillance
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – The Plateau State Government has reactivated isolation centres, intensified public awareness campaigns and strengthened disease surveillance as part of measures to prevent the spread of Ebola into the state. The state Commissioner for Health, Dr Nicholas Ba’amlong, disclosed this during a press briefing, saying the government had also directed its emergency preparedness team to assess safety measures at the airport and alert local government areas bordering neighbouring states. “Residents should maintain proper hygiene and avoid contact with potentially infected persons,” Ba’amlong said. “Maintain good hygiene, wash your hands regularly and avoid direct contact with the blood and body fluids of suspected infected persons,” he urged. “Remain vigilant and report suspected cases to health authorities,” the commissioner said, stressing that public cooperation was critical to preventing the spread of the disease.” ” The measures were announced alongside 10 resolutions approved at the 12th Plateau State Council on Health meeting held last week “ “The resolutions include establishing a state health trust fund, strengthening disease surveillance, addressing shortages of health workers and establishing an emergency fund for public health threats,” Ba’amlong said. He added, “These measures are aimed at strengthening the state’s preparedness to respond to disease outbreaks and improving the delivery of healthcare services to residents.” The commissioner urged residents to “follow public health guidance and report suspected cases promptly to health authorities.” The post Ebola: Plateau reactivates isolation centres, strengthens surveillance appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: TenTrade in Lagos: A conversation about education and the future of trading
item.description: Ahead of TenTrade’s “One Community, One Future” seminar on November 7th, we spoke with Andreas Andreou, Partner & Chief Revenue Officer; Obasi Wilfred, Regional Director, Africa; and Ademola Adeagbo, Head of Education, Africa. Together, they discuss what traders need to learn, how mentors can help and what building a trading community means in practice. Q: What does “One Community, One Future” mean to you? Andreas Andreou: It expresses the kind of company we want TenTrade to become. A global business needs more than a presence in different markets, it needs meaningful relationships within them. For us, bringing educators, mentors and traders together is part of building those relationships. Obasi Wilfred: For me, the important word is “community.” Our work in Africa has to reflect the people here, their questions, circumstances and ambitions. Community means having a two-way conversation and allowing what we hear locally to influence how we support traders. Ademola Adeagbo: I see it as creating an environment where learning is an ongoing conversation. You can attend a presentation and understand a concept, then struggle when you try to apply it. Having access to educators and mentors gives you somewhere to bring those questions. That is the value I want people to see. Q: Why Lagos, and why now? Andreas Andreou: If we want a lasting presence in Africa, we need to invest time in meeting people and understanding their expectations. Lagos gives us an opportunity to do that in person. The decision to hold this event reflects the direction we want to take, which is building our presence through education and relationships. Obasi Wilfred: Lagos is a starting point. Nigeria matters in our regional thinking in its own right, and we want to understand what traders here need rather than approach Africa as one single market. Meeting people allows us to hear the details behind a request for “more education”, which topics need explaining and what makes learning difficult. Ademola Adeagbo: From my side, the reason to bring people together is the quality of the learning we can do face to face. A participant can ask a question and work through an example with an educator. We can move beyond defining risk management to discussing how someone would actually apply it. That is what makes an in-person seminar worth it. Q: How would you describe the Nigerian trader today, and what do they need most? Andreas Andreou: From a company perspective, I would be cautious about putting every Nigerian trader into one category. We need to serve people at different stages of experience without assuming they all want the same thing. That requires clear information. Our global experience gives us a foundation, but our regional team helps us understand how to make that useful locally. Obasi Wilfred: I would describe a range of people rather than a single profile.
